summary.text: A 22-year-old girl with a broken heart problem reported hopelessness, depression and suicidal ideation after breaking up with her boyfriend because she was being cheated on. She had always failed to move on, was not excited about daily activities, kept remembering events with her lover and felt her life had no meaning. She had previously received counseling from colleagues, with some but not full relief. She was described as a nonvoluntarily-referred patient.

In single-session rapid tele-psychotherapy with music therapy she chose a song representing her feelings, gave informed consent, heard sedative music and rated her hopelessness, depression and suicidal ideation at 8. She set goals, answered miracle questions, sang her chosen song and wrote more positive lyrics, stated intentions to change, and at the closing stage received motivation and support and scored 6.

After 9 months she reported a score of 2, felt as if she had a new life, no longer had negative feelings or thought about her earlier problems, could focus on herself, had a new job and was more involved in religious activities. Using the soundtrack of her life as a lifelong reminder was recommended. The scores came from verbal 0-10 self-ratings and the sources disagree on whether the instrument was validated.
